rdf:Description.dc:description: From 1961 to 1971, Whitney Young was the Executive Director of the National Urban League (NUL), a civil rights organization which emphasizes economic parity and self-reliance. In March 1963, A. Philip Randolph asked Young and the NUL to participate in a proposed March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom to be held in August. Young agreed and became one of the organizers of the March, known as the Big Six.
